rubrics.justification: The response appropriately identifies a very poor-quality early blastocyst consistent with the reported 0DD grade, noting limited expansion and absent/degenerative ICM and TE. It adds reasonable caveats about single-image limitations, though some visual details like collapse/focus issues are somewhat speculative.

It integrates age, ovarian reserve, prior live birth, endometrial thickness, male factor, smoking, BMI, and prior cycle history well, and clearly explains how these modify prognosis relative to the poor embryo morphology.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent: embryo quality is treated as the dominant negative factor while younger age and favorable reserve modestly offset prognosis. Minor imprecision appears when distinguishing implantation, clinical pregnancy, and live birth probabilities.

The assessment is broadly aligned with Gardner grading interpretation and standard IVF counseling principles, including emphasis on embryo quality, smoking cessation, and review of sperm/uterine factors after failure. Some recommendations (e.g., adjunct sperm selection methods, progesterone specifics) are more clinic-dependent than guideline-mandated.

It provides clear practical next steps for the current transfer and future planning, including counseling expectations, luteal support review, lifestyle optimization, embryology review, sperm DNA fragmentation consideration, and uterine reassessment if needed.
